P1.evidence: No setter code in the title and no application referenced, so the read-back does not apply. The usual three-part frame, delivered twice because of a connection drop: 'It's just an opportunity for me to understand you, right? Where are you today? Where do you want to be if we can help? There's so many options that we can recommend. Okay?' — no 'what's in the way'. Agreement was the trailing 'Okay?' answered 'Okay'. The open question ran cleanly: 'How can we potentially help you, my friend?'

P2.evidence: Nothing ran. No age, no height, no weight. The occupation — thirteen years in the Army, a Ranger School graduate three months out from Regiment selection — was volunteered and never asked about beyond a friendly aside about the SEALs. No health, injury or limitation question. No training week, despite 'I work out like almost every day' sitting there unexplored. Most striking are diet and sleep: the prospect described a sustained several-thousand-calorie daily deficit and severe sleep restriction with substantial muscle loss, finishing two weeks earlier, and neither was picked up. Those two facts are the entire physiological context for what he is asking for, and the rep asked no follow-up on either.

P3.evidence: The bridge was attempted three times and never landed. 'Why do you even need this?', 'why is that an issue for you?', and 'Are you hoping to get to the next level or push yourself? Like, what is really the objective?' produced 'I guess I don't know what you're trying to ask' and then 'No, it's just a program, I guess.' Repeating the same question in the same register three times without changing the angle is why it failed. The one concrete thread available was handed over unprompted — 'I just, so like, I don't know, I got two kids' — and was never touched. Nothing on aesthetics, function, mobility, strength, energy, ripple effects, who else it impacts, or identity.

P4.evidence: The self-sufficiency challenge ran almost verbatim: 'there's ChatGPT, YouTube, information is so abundant now. Why haven't you been able to piece together your own workout?' It is the correct scripted move and here it backfired — the prospect agreed with it against his own purchase: 'nah, you're right. I should be able to.' The script assumes the answer exposes a structural gap; with a capable, disciplined buyer it instead hands him the reason not to buy. He did partially name his own gap afterwards — 'it's one thing to plan the program, and it's another thing to execute it. I feel like it's just harder for me to plan it' — but the rep did not build on it. Past attempts were never asked about at all.

P5.evidence: No consequence was established anywhere. No two-year question, no settle-for, no why-not. The only move was the route A / route B frame at the end: 'you have two paths in front of you, dude. You can either kind of scramble and try and put together your own structure, or you can utilize a structure which is proven, tried and tested... Which path do you feel like is ultimately going to best serve you when it comes to preparing yourself for selection?' Correct move, no ground beneath it, and it produced exactly the answer an unprepared frame produces: 'Something I got to think about for sure.'

P6.evidence: Not attempted in any form. No trust gauge, no capability check, no all-in question. The lower-tier product was screen-shared and priced within two minutes of the prospect's opening answer, with the only check being 'Does this feel like it's going to be what you're kind of looking for?' — answered 'Yeah, I think along those lines, I'd have to consider it, but yeah', which is not a yes and was treated as one.

P11.evidence: No sale of any kind, so payment, the Trevor booking, the agreement and the onboarding sequence were all unreachable. A Primal University link was texted to the prospect's phone at his request, which is not part of this phase.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger landed twice and cleanly — 'I'd have to consider it' at 00:06:46 and 'Something I got to think about for sure' at 00:10:55 — and not one move of the play was attempted. The complete response was 'Okay. No worries, brother. I mean, we're always going to be here.' No 'do you feel this can get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', and no attempt to book a next contact. Given the prospect has a hard, dated deadline three months out, 'what's your plan between now and selection?' was available and free.

SCRIPT GAP — the prospect who already has free professional coaching. This is the sharpest version of the cheaper-alternative gap in the corpus, because the alternative is not cheaper, it is free and institutional: 'I have strength coaches, I have nutrition coaches that are already like assigned to my unit and whatnot. So I kind of have that face to face coaching already' plus 'I have access to free gyms.' There is no play for differentiating against embedded professional support the buyer already receives, and the rep did not attempt one — he answered 'Makes sense, brother' and moved to the lower tier. Any prospect in the military, in professional sport, or in an employer with an on-site programme will present this identically.

SCRIPT GAP — the buyer who wants a fixed-duration artefact rather than a coaching relationship. He asked for it precisely in his first sentence: 'a program that I can follow for, like, maybe, you know, a month or two', tied to a selection date roughly three months out. The product line runs 3, 6 and 12 months of coaching or an open-ended monthly subscription; there is no defined-block preparation product and no scripted way to reshape the offer into one. The rep's only available move was to route him to the subscription and hope he treats it as a one-month purchase, which is exactly what he described doing.

notes: Twelve minutes and effectively no process. The prospect declined coaching in his opening sentence and the rep accepted that framing rather than testing it, so Baseline, Goals, Consequence and Commitment never ran and none of the three pillars was ever presented. Two specific things to correct. First, do not offer the prospect the free-alternative argument: 'there's ChatGPT, YouTube, information is so abundant now' was said by the rep and agreed with by the prospect, and it de-sold the call in one exchange. Second, when the bridge question fails, change the angle rather than repeating it — asking 'why do you even need this?' three times to a man who had just mentioned two children and a selection date three months away left both of the real levers untouched.
